fields.description:
Enable a self-contained, standard rebar MCP HTTP server on the AWS box (which runs Gerrit +
review-bot + opcert) so the copilot, codex, and claude clients drive ALL rebar operations through
it (dogfooding), with setup matching the user-facing docs. Design settled via /rebar-brainstorm and
operator-approved 2026-08-24 — see the "OPERATOR-APPROVED DESIGN" comment for the full rationale and
the AWS-cost analysis. Summary of the settled design:
- Exposure/auth: nginx `/mcp/` TLS edge → loopback-bound `rebar-mcp` HTTP; `static` verifier with
  per-client bearer PATs. Claude's static-bearer path is verified by rebar's own docs
  (`docs/mcp-auth.md` §4); Copilot (`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` `headers`) and Codex
  (`~/.codex/config.toml` `bearer_token_env_var` / `http_headers`) static-bearer-over-HTTP are
  verified against those tools' current official docs (research 2026-08-24; citations recorded in the
  ADR). None of the three requires OAuth.
- Autodeploy: blue-green immutable-release (immutable release + atomic nginx-upstream flip +
  retire-when-idle with retention/cap/alert), NOT the review-bot stop-and-drain. The rationale is
  self-contained: a shared, never-idle MCP server saturates a gauge-gated drain bound (review-bot bug
  7b4a) and would kill an in-flight certified op, whereas blue-green decouples retirement from the
  deploy. (The operator's LOCAL `origin/main`-tracking updater is cited in the ADR as external
  operational prior art for the immutable-release/atomic-pointer-swap pattern; it is a local tool,
  not an in-tree module, so the design does not depend on it being in the repo.)
- Certified-op routing: the MCP server signs op-certs under the box's EXISTING opcert signing
  environment — env_id `9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65` (the UUID pinned in
  `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` on `main`; `nava-opcert-prod` is only that key's comment/label),
  set via `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID`. No new env_id; certs verify against that already-pinned pubkey. The
  enforceable lane this enables is specifically the **completion-verifier** kind: `verify-opcert` (the
  merge-gate) enforces completion-verifier certs on closed tickets when `verify.require_environment`
  is set to that env_id — a single-valued config enablement that PRESERVES ADR 0049's single-env model
  (NOT the multi-valued change a distinct MCP env would require). Plan-review certs are also minted
  under the same env (trusted wherever consumed, e.g. the claim/plan-review gate), but they are NOT
  the lane `require_environment` enforces — do not claim otherwise. The committed `rebar.toml` does
  not currently set `verify.require_environment` (so the completion-verifier env-binding check is
  advisory today, exit 0). **Committing the flip (`verify.require_environment` +
  `verify.opcert_enforce_since`) into the authoritative `rebar.toml` is OUT OF SCOPE for this epic** —
  a deferred operator step, because a local-CLI close signs the completion-verifier cert under the
  LOCAL env (not `9f1c8e42`), so an early flip would fail `verify-identity` for every local close
  repo-wide. In scope (goose): the MCP container SIGNS under the existing `9f1c8e42` env, the joint
  enforce/grandfather MECHANISM is proven by a fixture `verify-opcert` test, and a runbook documents
  the deferred flip. Code review stays the Gerrit `LLM-Review` vote (no new op-cert kind);
  opcert/remote-cert coexist.

## Decomposition (8 children; ADR blocks all; dependency-ordered)
1. deft-evolutive-mosasaur — ADR (exposure/auth + blue-green drain + certified-op routing) + ADR
   0079 amendment. Blocks all.
2. cibophobic-holohedral-esok — infra: mcp compose svc + Dockerfile.mcp + nginx `/mcp/` switchable
   upstream **carried in the committed `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`** (the flip mutates config
   through that committed mechanism — e.g. a template-referenced upstream include — not out-of-band
   drift) + `/health` in-flight gauge + SIGTERM grace. dep: mosasaur.
3. panicky-sylphish-foxterrier — autodeploy: mcp blue-green target (build→cutover→retire). deps:
   mosasaur, esok.
4. exuberant-blockish-avians — secrets: SSM-materialized per-client bearer PATs (the SSM parameter
   is added to the terraform-managed `rebar_secret_params` set in `ssm.tf` — reproducible/teardownable
   as-code) + gitignored client-cred template + committed-secret guard. dep: mosasaur.
5. spoiled-bionic-goose — provision the MCP container to sign under the box's EXISTING opcert env
   (env_id `9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65` via `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID`; no new env/key), and
   prove the **completion-verifier** enforce/grandfather MECHANISM (joint `verify.require_environment`
   + `verify.opcert_enforce_since`) via a fixture-config `verify-opcert` test + a runbook for the
   deferred authoritative flip. **Actually committing the flip into the authoritative `rebar.toml`
   is OUT OF SCOPE — a deferred operator step (see the certified-op routing note above).** dep:
   mosasaur.
6. unmythical-uninspired-olm — client cfg: copilot/codex/claude static-bearer configs (exact
   config-file keys pinned from OBSERVED current client docs). deps: esok, avians.
7. inadequate-hydrated-starling — guidance/docs: AGENTS.md MCP-required policy + certified-op
   wording fix + docs/mcp-auth.md AWS recipe + client guide. deps: mosasaur, spoiled-bionic-goose,
   olm (olm settles the three client config shapes this guidance documents).
8. creased-childlike-jackal — approval-gated live 3-client prod verification (operator-performed).
   dep: olm.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The ADR (deft-evolutive-mosasaur) is landed on `main` deciding exposure/auth + blue-green
  drain + certified-op routing, with an ADR 0079 amendment. Checked: the ADR file exists on `main`.
- [ ] The mcp HTTP service + nginx `/mcp/` switchable upstream + `/health` gauge land (esok).
  Checked: the mcp service boots healthy fail-closed in compose and `/health` returns `in_flight`.
- [ ] The autodeploy blue-green mcp target lands (foxterrier). Checked: an mcp-only source change
  triggers a cutover, independent of review-bot/gerrit, without killing an in-flight op.
- [ ] Per-client bearer PATs are SSM-materialized (as-code in `ssm.tf`) + gitignored (avians); the
  MCP container signs under the box's existing opcert env (env_id `9f1c8e42-…`), the joint
  `verify.require_environment` + `verify.opcert_enforce_since` enforce/grandfather MECHANISM is proven
  by a fixture-config `verify-opcert` test, and a runbook documents the deferred authoritative flip
  (spoiled-bionic-goose; no new env; **committing the flip into the authoritative `rebar.toml` is OUT
  OF SCOPE for this epic — a deferred operator step**); and the three client configs connect (olm).
  Checked: committed-secret guard test green; a fixture-config `verify-opcert` test shows a
  post-boundary close without a completion-verifier cert FAILs while a pre-boundary close is advisory;
  the deferred-flip runbook exists; each client lists the rebar server and runs a basic read tool.
- [ ] Guidance + docs are updated (starling): AGENTS.md MCP-required policy + certified-op wording
  correction + docs/mcp-auth.md AWS recipe + client-connection guide. Checked: `grep` shows the new
  policy and no reference to a nonexistent code-review op-cert.
- [ ] Live verification (jackal, operator-performed): copilot/codex/claude each execute a basic
  rebar MCP command against the live endpoint, recorded on the jackal ticket.
- [ ] Every child ticket is closed. Checked: `rebar list-descendants jira-reb-3527` shows all
  descendants closed.

## Testing
Tier: **epic integration** — the epic has no standalone test of its own; its oracle is the aggregate
of its children's gated verification. Each code slice lands `Verified +1` through Gerrit CI carrying
its own tier-appropriate tests (compose/CLI integration for esok, subprocess/git integration for
foxterrier, file/guard tests for avians, signing round-trip for goose, client-connection smoke for
olm), the ADR/guidance slices verify by inspection, and the operator-run live 3-client smoke (jackal)
is the end-to-end oracle. The epic closes only when every child is closed on its own evidence and the
live verification is recorded.
